Subject: Private footprint migration + staggered cluster add (renewal-linked tradeoffs)

Alex / team —

Thanks again for the renewal conversation yesterday. Per our discussion, Biomedica is interested in converting the upcoming renewal into a renewal + expansion: two isolated analytics clusters (VPC, private control plane) to support the new analytics tenant and an on-prem satellite for sensitive workloads. High-level asks: 2 additional clusters (each ~4 A100-equivalent GPUs), dedicated KV cache per cluster, and geo-aware routing so analytic jobs run in the new private clusters.

We think a 24-month commitment gives the best unit economics for you; that would let us offer the price profile below in the attached "proposed-ma-points.pdf" and a draft capacity schedule in "capacity-plan.xlsx". Key constraints from our side:
- We need a firm order decision by end of May to hit Q3 provisioning windows for the satellite site.
- Migration of existing analytic traffic to the new clusters will need two one-week staging windows (non-overlapping) to validate KV cache warmups.

Can you confirm: procurement timeline, any org approvals we should loop in, and whether Biomedica prefers a single 24-month term vs a 12+12 option? I'll loop in Sales to get a formal MAP document ready.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Director, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: proposed-ma-points.pdf (summary), capacity-plan.xlsx (phases + sizing)

Naomi —

Appreciate the summary. A few clarifying points from my side:
1) Procurement timeline: procurement will evaluate commercial terms this month; final approval is likely by 05/30 if pricing and SLAs are clear.
2) Compliance: can you send SOC2/ISO evidence and the private deployment checklist? IT Ops will need the SOC2 report and encryption/KMS details.
3) Cost split: can you provide a line-item view for the satellite on-prem installation vs the VPC clusters (one-time vs recurring)? That helps our capital approval path.

If you can share the SOC2 pack and the one-pager cost breakouts, I will surface to security and procurement today. Also cc'ing our IT contact for tunnel and peering questions.

Best,
Alex Wu

alex.wu@biomedica.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-05-12T08:45:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Private footprint migration + staggered cluster add (renewal-linked tradeoffs)

Alex / Naomi —

Quick technical note from infra: phasing the two clusters across two quarters is feasible and recommended given KV cache warmup times. Suggested rollout:
- Phase 1 (Q3): spin up Cluster-A (VPC private tenant) + network peering; route 20% analytic jobs for shadow tests.
- Phase 2 (Q4): Cluster-B (VPC isolated analytics) and the on-prem satellite (airgapped install) with ramped cutover.

Network considerations:
- On-prem satellite will require an IPsec tunnel and static BGP for failover. We will provide a "network-reqs.txt" with ports and MTU recommendations (attached).
- KV cache behavior: warmup needs ~48–72 hours at representative load; suggest a staged cache prepopulate window.

Operationally we can support a single maintenance window per cluster per week during the stage, but no more than 2 hours/week for production-critical pipelines. Let me know if Biomedica's runbooks mandate additional blackout windows.

Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Attachment: network-reqs.txt

Alex —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. I attached the SOC2 pack to a secure folder (link below) and included a line-item breakout in the MAP draft. High level commercial proposal:
- 24-month committed term (preferred): 15% renewal credit off current ARR, plus volume tier pricing for the two new clusters.
- 12+12: smaller upfront concession (8%) but allows earlier exit after 12 months.

If procurement can sign by 05/30 we can preserve the Q3 provisioning window; otherwise the on-prem installation will likely slip into Q4 which pushes invoice recognition. I've also added a short mutual action plan (MAP-draft.docx) to the Drive link: please review items 3 (tunnel handoff) and 5 (acceptance criteria).

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Biomedica-MAP-7432

If procurement needs a formal procurement checklist or a sample order form, Marissa can drop the redline-ready amendment.

Thanks,
Naomi
